source_reviews.independent_solution: Copper, silver and brass satisfy the stated wetting requirement; stainless steel, aluminum and chromium do not. Wetting allows molten tin to spread and make the needed contact with a substrate. This is only the wetting prerequisite under the supplied temperature and surface conditions, not a sufficient proof of joint quality, a universal material classification or an instruction to solder.

For the requested outward movement, introduce the lower-surface-tension pure gasoline at the center. With radial coordinate increasing outward, a low-tension center and higher-tension grease-containing outer film give an outward surface-tension gradient and surface traction toward the higher-tension region. Reversing that arrangement by wetting the edge produces an inward-directed surface traction in this ideal connected-film picture. This predicts the direction of the surface-driven contribution under the given inequality; it is not a guarantee of complete stain removal, a general gasoline/grease property rule or permission to use gasoline.

The equilibrium drop is spherical. Equal densities remove the differential gravitational body force that would deform the drop relative to the surrounding fluid; they do not remove the oil-solution interface. For a fixed volume V of an immiscible, detached drop with uniform positive interfacial tension gamma, minimizing interfacial energy gamma*A minimizes area, and a sphere has the least area for V. Wall contact, nonuniform tension, motion or density mismatch would change the model. This is an analysis of Plateau's historical experiment, not Plato and not an experiment performed here.

The final temperature is higher under the stipulated isolated, fixed-mass, equilibrated model. For initial spherical drops with radii r_i, R^3=sum(r_i^3) after coalescence and A_before=4*pi*sum(r_i^2)>A_after=4*pi*(sum(r_i^3))^(2/3) for more than one nonzero drop. The decrease in surface energy supplies the increase in thermal internal energy when external transfer/work and other energy changes are excluded and transient motion has dissipated. With constant gamma and specific heat c as an additional approximation, m*c*(T_after-T_before)=gamma*(A_before-A_after)>0. No numerical temperature increase is determined. In a real nonisolated process not all surface-energy release need heat the mercury. Do not handle mercury.

A spherical thin soap film has two interfaces: p_inside-p_outside=4*gamma/r. Equal external pressures and constant equal gamma therefore give p_small>p_large for r_small<r_large. Air initially flows from the smaller bubble into the larger. As the smaller loses air, its radius decreases and its excess pressure increases, while the growing larger bubble's excess pressure decreases; the ideal unequal-bubble trajectory does not approach equal positive radii. It persists until the smaller bubble disappears or a stated model condition ceases to hold. Equal pressures would be a no-flow condition if both bubbles existed with equal radii, but not the predicted endpoint of this unequal-radius trajectory. Adult-guided low-risk testing is a separate required written task: record predictions, equipment/conditions, actual observations and unfinished steps honestly; no experiment has been done by this reviewer, and real film gamma can change.

For static rise in a uniform capillary, rho*g*h=2*gamma*cos(theta)/r. Complete wetting gives cos(theta)=1. Using the same r and g for both liquids yields rho_a/rho_w=(gamma_a/gamma_w)*(h_w/h_a)=(gamma_a/gamma_w)*(146/55), so rho_a=rho_w*(gamma_a/gamma_w)*(146/55). The millimeter units cancel in the ratio. Heights alone cannot give a unique alcohol density: require matched-temperature surface tensions of the specified alcohol composition and water and the water density. Neither rho_a=rho_w nor rho_a/rho_w=146/55 follows without the tension ratio. No arbitrary property values, composition, contact angle or temperature may be supplied.

all_written_task_requirements.requirements: Give several surface-tension examples not discussed in the chapter and explain the mechanism in each. Sourced examples are acceptable; do not fabricate personal observation. Establishing that an example is new to the chapter requires chapter context not supplied in this blind source phase.

Actually compare sugar solution, soap solution and pure water with adult guidance, clean plastic vessels and suitable low-risk apparatus. Specify common temperature, solute identities/composition and concentrations, and comparable measurement procedures. A soap surfactant often lowers tension, whereas any sugar prediction is composition/temperature/concentration conditional. Predictions are not measured results. Record real measurements/observations, incomplete work and uncertainty; do not generalize one result to all solutions.

Classify only the supplied metals by the given wetting prerequisite for tin soldering; preserve temperature and surface-state scope, distinguish necessary from sufficient conditions, and require no actual soldering.

Explain why a wet glove may resist removal when a wetting liquid film exists between a fitted glove and skin. Discuss liquid bridges/contact and their surface-energy or capillary contribution, not a universal assertion about every glove or wetness. A quantitative pressure or friction claim would need meniscus/contact geometry and material data.

Select center or edge for outward surface-driven grease migration using the supplied higher tension of grease-in-gasoline, equal temperature and a connected film. Preserve this conditional historical theoretical model and explicit prohibition of actual gasoline cleaning or experiments.

Explain that loosening the top layer can interrupt connected fine-pore capillary pathways feeding an evaporating surface, reducing that supply of water. Preserve conditional soil/pore/evaporation assumptions; do not claim every soil/environment benefits or invent field observations.

Derive the spherical equilibrium shape for a density-matched, immiscible, detached drop with uniform interfacial tension. Preserve the static model and Plateau historical attribution and no practical-performance requirement.

Infer warming from decreased surface energy only for the stated isolated mass, excluded external work/other stores and equilibrated endpoints. Distinguish real heat losses and transient motion; prohibit mercury contact/handling. No quantitative rise without additional property/geometry data.

Use the two-interface spherical soap-bubble pressure relation, constant equal gamma, common external pressure and an open air path to predict small-to-large flow and its endpoint. Then separately perform adult-guided low-risk verification, distinguish prediction from actual observation, record conditions and unfinished steps, and allow composition/process-dependent real-film gamma. Do not fabricate experimental confirmation.

Derive the alcohol-density ratio from 55 mm and 146 mm rises with the same tube, temperature, equilibrium and complete wetting. Explicitly retain missing matched-temperature tension values, water density and alcohol composition/temperature. Heights alone are underdetermining; fabricate no numbers.

For the initially water-filled vertical tube of radius 0.8 mm, identify the missing end states, meniscus shapes/contact angles, outside pressures and liquid-column boundaries before assigning a remaining mass. Hydrostatic balance depends on the pressures imposed at both ends; radius alone cannot fix retained length or mass. Do not substitute a reservoir-fed capillary-rise formula or select open/closed ends without authorization.
